quest.title: One for the Foodies, Two for the Show
quest.description: Paimon, ever-gluttonous, pulls you over to Wanmin Restaurant for a good meal. There, you happen to meet Xiangling, who is deep in thought...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x60, Hero's Wit x3, Mora x30000

chapter.title: One for the Foodies, Two for the Show

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, guess who's here~!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sorry to bother you...

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Oh, no way! It's the Traveler, and Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Chef Mao
dialogues.text: Ah, Traveler, welcome! Good to see you. What can I get for you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We want some Black-Back Perch Stew!

dialogues.speaker: Chef Mao
dialogues.text: Alright, Black-Back Perch Stew it is! Make yourselves at home, it'll be right out for you in just a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Thanks, Chef Mao!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: I was just thinking about you guys, and now you're here! It feels like you heard my call and came running, tee-hee.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You mean, you were about to come looking for us?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Uh-huh, there's something I wanna discuss with you guys. Did you happen to see how the city looked on the way over here? Everyone's getting ready for the Moonchase Festival!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Oh, so that's what it's called.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Moonchase Festival? Is that another one of Liyue's ancient traditions?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: That's right! Moonchase is a big festival where we celebrate the arrival of the fall by moonlight. The old folks say that thousands of years ago, this was the time of year when the adepti would seek the Way.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: But it's completely different nowadays. We eat our favorite foods, spend time with friends and relatives, enjoy the moon and the flowers... so much easier. Basically, we just do all the things that people like doing and don't take a whole lot of effort.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like Paimon's kind of festival!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: *chuckle* With your great taste in food, Moonchase Festival is sure to be to your liking!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! If you've got a problem with Paimon's taste, just spit it out!

response.speaker: Xiangling
response.text: Um, so are you guys free these days? I'm taking part in this year's Masterful Chefs. If possible, I'd like you to be my culinary consultants!

response.speaker: Chef Mao
response.text: That's right! Getting some suggestions from friends will broaden your horizons!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Masterful Chefs, huh? So is that, like, a competition?

response.speaker: Xiangling
response.text: Oh right, yeah, I guess you probably haven't heard about it before.

response.speaker: Xiangling
response.text: Every year, Moonchase Festival has a different theme — usually picked by the Qixing. This year's theme is Feast of the Bounteous Land, so the Qixing decided to organize a cooking competition.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Feast of the Bounteous Land... pretty much sums up what Liyue's all about. Great theme!

response.speaker: Xiangling
response.text: I totally agree! I heard it was Ningguang that came up with it. She's so amazing... and so full of mystery.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So, what do you need us to do?

response.speaker: Xiangling
response.text: Well, I wanna take part in the competition, but coming up with new dishes is hard work. By the time you've finally thought of something, cooked it, taste-tested it... it can be hard to judge whether you're really onto something or not.

response.speaker: Xiangling
response.text: So I was thinking I could get the two of you to help by gathering everyone's thoughts on what makes a great dish! I really want to think outside the box this time, and to do that I'm gonna need lots of different ideas from lots of different people.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #This'll be a piece of cake! We've got friends from all over the map, haven't we, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Xiangling
response.text: Hee-hee, you sound pretty confident!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, y'know, not to brag or anything...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But first things first, let's have a delicious Wanmin meal... After that, we can go around all our friends in Liyue and get their ideas one by one.

response.speaker: Xiangling
response.text: Okay, great! Also, Guoba should be back soon, so we can all go together!

response.speaker: Chef Mao
response.text: Here's your Black-Back Perch Stew, folks!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mmm! It smells so good!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Thank you, Chef Mao.

response.speaker: Chef Mao
response.text: Haha, it's my pleasure.

response.speaker: Chef Mao
response.text: Xiangling can be a bit of a handful, so please look out for her while you're out and about.

response.speaker: Xiangling
response.text: C'mon Dad! Why would you say that!?

response.speaker: Chef Mao
response.text: Because I know you all too well, my dear, that's why. You mustn't be quite so reckless when you're out in the wild, you understand? You'd do well to be a little more cautious, like our Traveler friend.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't worry, we're all friends here. Let's all look out for each other!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mmm... That was so delicious! Theory confirmed, this is definitely chili pepper weather!

response.speaker: Xiangling
response.text: Ah! And Guoba's back! Roly-polying around, as usual.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, let's pack up and head out!

talks.objective: Look for some friends to chat with in the city

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So it's outside-the-box thinking that we're looking for, right? Hu Tao always seems to have a unique perspective, so let's make this our first stop!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: What what what? My ears are burning... did somebody say my name?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Aiya, it's Paimon and the Traveler! And Xiangling too!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We've come to hang out!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Of course, Hu Tao! Way, way outside the box!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Meaning... you're here for some other reason, right? How might I be of assistance?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Well, Hu Tao, I wanted to ask you: What kind of food do you like?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: What food I like? Hmm... off the top of my head, I don't really have an answer.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, so even Hu Tao gets lost for words sometimes. Paimon sure didn't see that coming.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Come on, even the chirpiest birds clock out for the night, right? I'm no different.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Pretty sure "clocking out" isn't something birds do, but okay...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's okay, Hu Tao, just keep it simple.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Right! There's no need to over complicate it, just pick a dish and tell me what you like about it! I'm doing some market research.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: I see, I see! Launching a new dish? Well, let me say right off the bat — nothing weird, okay! Some poached fish, a side of shrimp dumplings, that's all you need!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Poached fish and shrimp dumplings? That's a bit ordinary, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Well, it is and it isn't. Think about it, poached fish is hot and spicy with a powerful aroma. It's a "dynamic" dish. Add a side of shrimp dumplings, and there's your "static" component. Got it?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Dynamic...?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Oh, oh.... I—I can do dynamic! Mushroom Slime Stew—

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Not that kind of dynamic! A dish is more than substance, it's a mood. Poached fish is red and spicy. It elicits a response from the eyes, ears, nose, and mouth. That's why I call it "dynamic."

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Shrimp dumplings are more subdued — clear and smooth with a pure and subtle fragrance. I call that "static." Combining dynamic and static is how you create a perfectly balanced meal, a union between opposite but complementary features co-existing in perfect harmony!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon didn't follow that at all... but at the same time, it kinda sounded smart, so...

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Okay... dynamic and static, opposite but complementary...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, is this just another way of saying you should keep everything balanced? Y'know, a little meat, a little veggie? A little salt, a little sugar?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Bingo! Except, I don't think you need to have a sweet dish for it to be a complete meal. Personally, I always skip dessert.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Okay, I think I got it! At first, I thought you were just goofing around, but actually you make a really good point!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Hee-hee, how did I ever doubt you, Hu Tao! Thanks!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: When it comes to telling tales, the storytellers have got nothing on Hu Tao.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Hmm? Sounds suspiciously like a compliment to me. I'll take it!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're clearly a keen philosopher.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Aha! Well, at least one of you gets it!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Everything in this world runs on its own set of principles, be it the circle of life or sugar and spice! You either get it or you don't.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Since the Traveler seems to approve, I'll make sure to factor it in.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon thinks we're pretty much done here now. Let's head to Bubu Pharmacy next.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Bubu Pharmacy... Yeah, you'll definitely get some interesting responses over there. Hehehe...

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you. Is everything okay?

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: Why, if it isn't the special guests who seldom visit. Less busy than usual, I see.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yikes, wh—what happened to Baizhu's voice!?

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: Sss! Excuse me! The neck!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... it's just Changsheng...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's been a while.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Haha, welcome, welcome. Here to procure an herbal remedy, I presume?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No no, we actually came for the conversation this time. We're here to talk food!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: I'm entering this year's cooking competition, so I wanted to ask you both... wait, there's three of you! I wanted to ask the three of you about what kind of food you like.

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: Hahaha, most astutely self-corrected. We shall surely supply our assistance.

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: You need to know... what food I like? Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: It's all the same. No flavor.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Qiqi has some gustatory dysfunction and can't taste any food. Make no mistake, she's not being uncooperative.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Oh, I understand, that's fine! Still, I'd expect Qiqi to have some sort of dietary preferences, though. There must be some dishes that you like the sensation of?

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: Sensation? Hmm... Yes. There's one.

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: Coconut milk... Nice and cold...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well that doesn't help us. It's not a dish, it's a drink...

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: How about you two? Any thoughts?

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: I like bite-sized morsels of meat.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: I agree with Changsheng.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Many of our patients are the elderly and young children. They find large chunks of Fowl or seafood difficult to swallow and digest. Dishes where the ingredients have been finely chopped, on the other hand, are far more suitable for them.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: We also see plenty of people with colds and sore throats who find it difficult to eat rich food... From a purely pharmaceutical perspective, I tend to recommend soups and stews.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Got it. Would that be medicinal soups and stews?

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: Whew, medicinal soup... I don't like it.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: I must apologize for having such a one-track mind... It's a little difficult to think about food without worrying about the health implications these days. We've had quite the endless stream of patients recently... If you ask me, I think the changing weather is to blame.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's okay, everyone's input counts. Keeping it seasonal and suitable for all ages sounds like a pretty good idea to Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Important considerations for any chef.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Medicinal dishes have higher demands in terms of nutritional balance than the kind of food I normally cook. I don't usually focus on medicinal properties, but since this is for a competition... maybe I can score more points by taking both flavor and function into account.

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: Food with substance, always better. Everyone will like it.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: It's a great suggestion! Thanks everyone!

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: You're welcome. As long as we could help.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: It's great to have a doctor's unique perspective. I'm feeling inspired!

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Oh, how you flatter me.

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: Receptivity to sensible suggestions makes for a savvy chef.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, she is! Creating new dishes is Xiangling's favorite thing to do, you can be sure she'll put lots of care and attention into it!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Hee-hee... Everyone's got their hobbies, and mine is cooking! Usually, I just go with my own ideas, but having a whole new perspective this time is sure to make a big difference to the end result.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Great! That makes this whole trip worth it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, time to move on to the next! So we've got an independent thinker's perspective and a health perspective... Next, Paimon thinks we should probably talk to some picky eaters.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Hmm? Oh, it's the Traveler and Paimon... and Xiangling.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Greetings, friends. It's been a while.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Hey! What brings you here?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Huh? Everyone's gathered together here...

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Has something happened?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's with this great big stone on the ground?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Long story... So, just to confirm, I will assume responsibility for handling this stone of unknown origin. Any objections?

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: None here. You know how to get things done, Keqing. As long as it's with you, I can rest easy knowing that it's in safe hands.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Should I take this to mean that you doubt the relative safety of leaving this in the hands of the Tianquan?

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Huh? Well, for starters, Keqing is the one who's always out running errands, rain or shine. Besides, you don't seem to give a wooden Mora about this whole thing anyway, so what's it to you!

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: I was merely joking. You, meanwhile, seem only too ready to pounce when an opportunity to publicly lambaste me arises, even when it means giving our poor mutual friend here the cold shoulder.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Uh... Is this a bad time?

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: By no means. You wish to know about the stone, I presume? Then let me invite the great seafarer, Captain Beidou, to tell the story — if she would be so kind.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: You... Ugh, fine...

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Well... It's a big one, right? And such a smooth surface, too. Makes you think there's gotta be a good chunk of jade in there.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: It was found by a fishing crew not far off the coast. It must have been underwater for years, so the erosion will be what's given it that smooth finish.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Finds like this cannot be kept as private property, and must be submitted to a holder of public office. Placing it into our custody will also give them peace of mind.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: So, what's inside it?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Well, we've hit it with just about every weapon we could get our hands on and haven't managed to even dent it yet. Clearly, there's more to it than meets the eye.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No weapon could smash it open? Wow... Paimon doesn't think we've ever encountered a stone like that before...

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Keqing has taken an unusually keen interest in this giant stone, which is why we are leaving the matter in her capable hands.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Let's put that aside for a second. Traveler, what brings you here? Were you looking for someone?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Actually, we were looking for all of you! We need all hands on deck here!

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Oh? Hopefully not because there's been some sort of cataclysmic event?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: No no, nothing like that! Paimon's just getting carried away... I just wanted to ask everyone about their food preferences.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: ...Food preferences? That's a little unexpected.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: I have rather simple tastes. Precise, pure, smart, and sophisticated. That is all I require.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: That's your idea of simple, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: I summed up my culinary requirements in four words. Is that insufficiently simple for you?

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: A few weeks out on the open ocean would fix your flawed definition of simplicity, let me tell you that.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: What about you, Beidou?

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Me? Uh... if it's freshly cooked and piping hot, that floats my boat. If it's got a little chili pepper in there too, I'm one very happy Captain.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon thought you would've said bar food.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Hahaha, oh, bar food works too!

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: As for me... it's got to be seafood.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Okay, got it! So, seafood, piping hot, and, uh, simple-but-sophisticated...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not a lot of overlap...

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: That's where I would disagree! Traveler, surely you've heard of Golden Shrimp Balls?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: (*gasp* Oh my... they're my favorite...)

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: You need to wash and de-vein the shrimp, wrap it in finely sliced potato strips, then deep fry it to perfection. There's no room for cutting corners!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: They're very precisely put together, they taste pure, the presentation is smart, and the skill needed to cook them is highly sophisticated... It fits Ningguang's four-word summary to the letter!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, so what you're saying is... for all the frills and trills, good food is all the same at the core?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: I heartily agree. Golden Shrimp Balls are a prime example. Their essence lies in combining art and nutrition in a single package. It is a dish of true value.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Okay, got it — so, Keqing loves Golden Shrimp Balls...

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: I—I didn't say that! ...Did I?

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Hahaha, no, at least not outright.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Alrighty! Thanks for all of your input! I'll be sure to take it all into consideration!

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Traveler, Paimon, do you have anything planned after this?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No immediate plans.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Good. I'd like you to help me investigate something. It's about this stone...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You picked the right people for the job. We investigate stuff all the time!

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: My thoughts exactly. The Qixing has a public duty to deliver our final verdict to the fisherman, but there are also some things I would like to investigate on a personal level.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: I'm sure you've become acquainted with the general background of the Moonchase Festival. However, I have my own understanding of this festival's roots.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: My grandfather was a researcher of Liyue's traditions. In his notes, he indicated that there was a deity called the Stove God in ancient Liyue which people paid tribute to at a certain time of the year.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Very few written records make mention of the Stove God, and those that do are notoriously confusing. Some scholars believe that the Stove God was just another title held by the Lord of Geo, but others suggest that this was a different deity altogether...

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: One folktale even claims that the ancients found the Stove God's shrine, but there was no statue — only a huge, smooth slab of stone.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Shortly after it was found, the stone was lost in transit, and it hasn't been seen since. This stone here has all the same features, so I suspect it could be the one that went missing all those years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: After many years of researching ancient texts, my grandfather came to believe that the practice of paying seasonal tribute to the Stove God may be best described as a festival — he called it the Stove God Festival. That would make it the forerunner to the Moonchase Festival we know today.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: But this is all just theory and conjecture. To prove any of it, we'd need to start by identifying who the Stove God really was.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Now that Rex Lapis has passed on and Liyue has entered the age of humankind, his successors should continue to respect our nation's culture and traditions, just as he did.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: That's why I think the responsibility for this situation should fall to me. It's a chance to shed light on our history, revitalize an ancient tradition, and possibly prove my grandfather's hypothesis along the way. With any luck, we'll nail all three in one fell swoop.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: It was just a couple of days ago that we received this stone — right after we decided to use food as the central theme for this year's festival. It makes me wonder... maybe a divine will is at work behind all of this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Three birds with one stone, huh? That's pretty efficient — even for Keqing!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'd love to help, but...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm in the middle of a commission for Xiangling...

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Hey, don't worry about that. This sounds super important, so don't mind me.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Besides, we were only... Hmm? Wait a second... I got it!!!

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Wh—What? Why are you shouting?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Keqing, can I tag along for your investigation?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Huh? But...

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Since it's all about the Stove God, I might get to learn something useful about cooking along the way. It'll be great inspiration for me in the competition!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Please? Lemme come along. I promise I'll help!

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: If it means that much to you... Okay, I suppose you can come.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Really!? Yay, thank you so much! You're the best!

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Ahem! Now that that's settled... Time to get going. Qingce Village is said to be home to a lot of historical texts, so I'd like to start by making some inquiries there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, then it's off to Qingce we go!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hi granny, we need your help with something!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are there any old books around in Qingce Village? You know, from a really long time ago.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: Oh, looking for ancient texts, are we? Let me think...

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: There is an old warehouse over there, property of the Feiyun Commerce Guild. Many books are stored inside — those that they have no room for at home. In fact, their youngest comes over this way to read sometimes.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: The Feiyun Commerce Guild's youngest? You must be talking about Xingqiu.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Paimon didn't know they had a warehouse here. Let's go take a look!

talks.objective: Go to the Feiyun Commerce Guild warehouse

dialogues.text: Oh, uh... you're all here...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That voice sounds familiar...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ganyu?

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: Sorry to interrupt your conversation... I was in the area buying a few things and I heard the disturbance, so I felt compelled to come take a look...

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: You mean Cloud Retainer? I saw her too. She just suddenly showed up right in the middle of the street... Whatever adeptal power that was, she certainly knows how to make an entrance.

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: Lady Keqing, you saw her too? ...Ahh!!!

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: Do you, uh, have a moment? I need to... discuss something with you.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: What is it, Ganyu? Has something urgent come up while I've been out?

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: No, it's nothing work-related. I wanted to ask about... um, something personal. Is that okay?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: (A personal matter... involving me? Surely I haven't done anything improper recently, have I?)

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: Please, Lady Keqing? This is really important to me...

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Oh, uh, okay.

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: I noticed Cloud Retainer was here for quite a while. Did she say anything about... m—me? When I was young?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: About your childhood? No, nothing at all.

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: What? Really!? Phew!!! Thank goodness...

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: I was getting really worried... Once she gets talking to people, she tends to go off on all sorts of tangents... so I was worried she might have bored you with some stories about me, heh...

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Your name didn't even come up. So you've nothing to worry about.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Keqing, how are you not asking a bunch of questions right now? There's obviously some juicy gossip here, aren't you curious to find out what it is?

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: Ah! P—Please, no, don't do that to me...

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Of course not. Whatever it is, I'm not curious, and I'm not going to ask.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: If Ganyu has a secret and she wishes to keep it that way, nobody should make it their business to try and get it out of her. That's just basic decency, is it not?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y—Yes, Ma'am... Paimon'll never bring it up again...

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: ...Keqing, I...

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: Thank you. You're so kind and considerate... I've always seen that in you.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Wh—What's that got to do with... Honestly. Go on, you should be getting back now.

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: Oh my, you're right, I should. Okay everyone, please excuse me, I should get back to work now. Take good care of Keqing for me.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Hey! What are you trying to say!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw, don't worry, Ganyu, we will!

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: Thanks. Hope to see you again soon.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: At the end there, she sounded like your big sister.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Ehh... just ignore her.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Hey everyone! I just had an idea!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: It only occurred to me when that adeptus showed up. Do you think the Stove God could be an adeptus too?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh! Could be!

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: I don't want to assert either way... but it seems highly likely.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: In that case, we should go ask the adepti about it. I think my master might be able to help.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Master? You mean, your teacher is an adeptus?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Uh-huh, she's over at Yujing Terrace. C'mon, I'll introduce you!

dialogues.speaker: Sheng
dialogues.text: Ugh... I've come here to clean the book warehouse plenty of times before, but this is the first time I've run into these crooks...

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Are you alright?

dialogues.speaker: Sheng
dialogues.text: I am, thanks to all of you. Hey, wait a minute — you're the Traveler, aren't you? And you're with... Lady Keqing! An honor, truly an honor!

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: We'll try not to take up too much of your time. I understand that this book warehouse is the property of the Feiyun Commerce Guild? Could you advise whether we might find any texts relating to the Stove God in this collection?

dialogues.speaker: Sheng
dialogues.text: The Stove God? Uh... I heard that's the Lord of Geo, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Really?

dialogues.speaker: Sheng
dialogues.text: Yeah, a friend of mine who conducts research mentioned it once before. We use stoves for cooking, and stoves are built from rock.

dialogues.speaker: Sheng
dialogues.text: Some people think that the stove is a gift from the Lord of Geo, and that's why they call him the Stove God.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Seems logical enough...

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: But do you have any books on the topic?

dialogues.speaker: Sheng
dialogues.text: Um... I, uh... I'm sorry, I'd have to ask the young master about that...

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Any questions? Please, ask away!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, it's Chongyun and Xingqiu!

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Hello, one and all.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Hey guys, what are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: I was bored with nothing to do and thought I'd come out this way for a bit of reading. And then I thought, why not bring Chongyun along, too.

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Yes, I'm just along for the ride really...

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: I see the Yuheng, Keqing, is with you. Whatever brings you here must surely be a matter of grave importance.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Master Xingqiu, if I may be so bold — do you happen to know if there are any texts on the subject of the Stove God among this collection?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Since I personally selected which volumes to store here, I do have some recollection of their contents.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: If my memory betrays me not, there is one volume among them called "Demystifying the Legends of Liyue," which mentions the Stove God.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Might I take a look?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Certainly. If it pleases my lady, I shall lead the way. Sheng, I will take care of things here. You're free to go about your own business.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They're back! So, did you find it?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Yes. Master Xingqiu has quite an exceptional memory, "Demystifying the Legends of Liyue" does indeed mention the Stove God. However...

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: It says the following: "The body of the dragon wielded a tail that could eclipse the sun, and claws to command fire and teach the ways of wisdom. Receiving the gift bequeathed unto them, humankind cooked food with fire, and thus did they prosper."

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: The body of a dragon? The stories about Rex Lapis say the same thing.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: That much is true. But this is the only passage in the whole book. If we want to find out more, we'll have to continue our investigation.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: There's nothing further to discover here. It seems we'll have to look at other options.

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: I come from a long lineage of exorcists, and our family too has amassed a number of ancient texts. Now that you mention the Stove God, I seem to recall reading somewhere that this god once appeared at the Guili Assembly. Of course, I can't say if it's true or not.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Books are penned by people. All they can do is show what the author was thinking. Everyone's mind is different, so every book on a given topic will give a different account.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: I apologize that we could not help in a more substantial capacity.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Your help thus far is quite ample. Liyue is a vast and rich land, all things that existed here in the past have left their trace. So long as we do not abandon our search, it is sure to bear fruit eventually.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Thank you all. We will continue our investigation elsewhere.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Ah, hold up! I had a question too! Xingqiu, Chongyun, could you tell me what kind of food you like?

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Food? Oh no... Y—You're not thinking of taking part in Masterful Chefs, are you!?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Uh, yeah, I totally am! What's wrong... You look like you've just seen a ghost!

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Xiangling, this is a major event. I beg you, please don't cook anything strange for this competition...

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: What do you mean, "strange"!?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Mushroom Slime Stew, to give one example.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Okay, fair enough, that dish isn't my most popular... but that's why I'm doing all this research, so I can create some really special dishes to win everyone over.

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Well, in that case... I like cold food.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's 'cause you can't handle hot and spicy, right?

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Haha, yes, you're absolutely right.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: My tastes are on the mild side — I prefer gentle dishes with minimal seasoning. Soups and stews, vegetables in broth, seafood or freshwater fish, either boiled or steamed... These kinds of dishes I am most partial to.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No surprises from Guhua Geek.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Okay, another mild child... Got it.

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: These are just personal preferences, and everyone's are quite different... Are you sure this eclectic mix of opinions will be of any use?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Of course! You're my customers, and putting a smile on customers' faces is my calling as a chef!

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Though Xiangling's market research blade stabs often into the dark, her heart never strays from the noble path.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If anyone can win hearts and minds with their cooking, it's gotta be someone like Xiangling. She's got pure intentions and really cares about the customers.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Where's all this praise coming from...? Knock it off guys, you're embarrassing me...

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Ah! Sorry for holding you all up — that's all I needed to know! Shall we carry on with the investigation now?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Over to you, Keqing. Where to next?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: So we've learned the Stove God allegedly made an appearance at the Guili Assembly. But today, that place is largely a wasteland, with few traces of human activity.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Wangshu Inn is close by, so let's stop off there on the way over and see what we can find out.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Forgive us, for this is where we must part ways. May your journey be a smooth one.

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Yes, best of luck! If you run into any difficulties, come and find us. We'll be only too glad to help!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thanks everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go! Next stop, Wangshu Inn!

talks.objective: Go to Wangshu Inn and look for Smiley Yanxiao

dialogues.speaker: Smiley Yanxiao
dialogues.text: Huh? Oh, Traveler. Who are all these people?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Friends of ours. Allow Paimon to introduce Xiangling, Guoba, and Keqing.

dialogues.speaker: Smiley Yanxiao
dialogues.text: Keqing? Of the Qixing!? She's the, um... the, uh...

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Hi.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No need to be so nervous, Yanxiao.

dialogues.speaker: Smiley Yanxiao
dialogues.text: It's not that, it's... I mean, I'm just your typical commoner, I've never met someone as high up as the Yuheng before in my whole life!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: (Look at that strong body, those powerful hands, and honest eyes... this guy must be a really great chef!)

dialogues.speaker: Smiley Yanxiao
dialogues.text: So, is there something I can help you with? You've come a long way out to end up at Wangshu Inn.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Let me fill you in...

dialogues.speaker: Smiley Yanxiao
dialogues.text: Okay, I see.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Legends claim that the Stove God once appeared at the Guili Assembly. As Wangshu Inn is the oldest extant building in this area, any historical texts from around these parts are likely to have ended up here.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Is there a room in this inn for storing books? And if there is, do any of them mention the Stove God?

dialogues.speaker: Smiley Yanxiao
dialogues.text: Now that you mention it, we do have a fair few ancient texts here. I remember looking through an old recipe book once... I just need to remember where they're all stored.

dialogues.speaker: Smiley Yanxiao
dialogues.text: If you're happy to wait here for a few minutes, I'll go have a look right away!

dialogues.speaker: Smiley Yanxiao
dialogues.text: Oh, Traveler, there's something I need to discuss with you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What is it? We need to pay up or something?

dialogues.speaker: Smiley Yanxiao
dialogues.text: What? No, I wouldn't take your money! We're all friends here. I just wanted to ask if you had the time to make a Satisfying Salad for me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A Satisfying Salad? What for?

response.speaker: Smiley Yanxiao
response.text: Guy who hangs out on the roof terrace, you know? Good looking fella, not too tall...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Shh! Don't you think he can hear you!?

response.speaker: Smiley Yanxiao
response.text: Oh, right! Uh, yeah, maybe. Anyway, you know who I mean.

response.speaker: Smiley Yanxiao
response.text: The boss told me to take care of him, but this guy, let me tell you — he is one tough nut to crack. He usually turns his nose up at everything that isn't Almond Tofu.

response.speaker: Smiley Yanxiao
response.text: But the boss tells me you once made him a Satisfying Salad and it all went down so well. So I was thinking... Could you teach me how to make it too? That way, I'll have something else in my arsenal.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, so this is for Xiao! You guys really look after him, huh.

response.speaker: Smiley Yanxiao
response.text: Well, that's life, right? You've gotta look out for your own people.

response.speaker: Smiley Yanxiao
response.text: Alright then — wait right here, I'll be just one minute!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Clock is ticking! 59, 58...

response.speaker: Keqing
response.text: Sorry for the trouble, Traveler.

response.speaker: Keqing
response.text: Okay.

response.speaker: Smiley Yanxiao
response.text: Here you are.

response.speaker: Keqing
response.text: Thank you ever so much.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: While Keqing's reading her book, let's make that Satisfying Salad! Xiangling, what are you gonna do?

response.speaker: Xiangling
response.text: I'd love to come watch too, but I don't wanna get in the way. So I'll just stay here with Keqing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay. Shall we go, then?

response.speaker: Smiley Yanxiao
response.text: Go ahead and get started, I'll just watch from over here! I only need to watch you make it once to have it committed to memory.

choices.text: Thanks for agreeing to dig out that book.
A certain person comes to mind...

dialogues.speaker: Smiley Yanxiao
dialogues.text: Alright, thanks for that. I think I've got it now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You got all the steps down, right?

dialogues.speaker: Smiley Yanxiao
dialogues.text: Of course. Don't forget, I am the best chef around these parts.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go see what Keqing and Xiangling are up to.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Keqing, Xiangling, we're back!

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: You've finished cooking? Good timing, we've finished our reading, too.

dialogues.speaker: Smiley Yanxiao
dialogues.text: And? Useful, or no?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Useful. There is a passage concerning the Stove God, and it's not what we were expecting.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: I quote: "60 miles to the northwest is the Guili Assembly. Many were settled there, where they hunted in groups, farmed the land, and made their living from what the soil yielded."

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: "When the Stove God descended, one god became many, all of which were the height of children. As does a star when it descends into the world, so the Stove God went out among the common folk and taught them to create fire. With fire, the people at last learned to make hot food, and they dined on rice congee and cooked meat thereafter."

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: This is a radically different account from the one given in "Demystifying the Legends of Liyue," and also a conflicting one.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "One god became many"... Does that mean there was more than one Stove God?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Taking the text at face value, that is what it says.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: "Went out among the common folk and taught them to create fire"... So, did the Stove God really go and teach people how to cook firsthand?

dialogues.speaker: Smiley Yanxiao
dialogues.text: Now that's a god who truly cared for their people.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So we've got two leads, but they contradict each other. How do we know which one to believe?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: By continuing with our investigation, and reserving judgment for now.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Thank you for this text, Yanxiao.

dialogues.speaker: Smiley Yanxiao
dialogues.text: It's my pleasure, really. Think nothing of it. If anything, I should be thanking the Traveler.

dialogues.speaker: Smiley Yanxiao
dialogues.text: Listen, you've helped me an awful lot — not just today but in the past, too. I wanna make it up to you properly, and as it happens, things are pretty quiet here today. So I'd like to take the chance to treat you all. What do you say — will you stay for a meal?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Wow, he sure sounds confident in his cooking! I like that — confidence is one of the best ingredients a chef can have!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: I really wanna try his cooking. I say we take him up on his offer!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Keqing, can you spare the time?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: It's hard to refuse a generous offer like that... Yes, I think we can fit this in.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Yanxiao, we await your culinary creations with great anticipation.

dialogues.speaker: Smiley Yanxiao
dialogues.text: Haha, I won't disappoint!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Everybody, please be seated!

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: You'd think you own the place.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: I'll sit here, with Guoba!

dialogues.speaker: Smiley Yanxiao
dialogues.text: Here we are. That's everything you ordered.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: (It all smells amazing... I think I've met my fellow finalist!)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mmmm~! It smells beauuuutiful!

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Strange, I never would have guessed that such a gifted chef worked here. This inn isn't particularly known for its food.

dialogues.speaker: Smiley Yanxiao
dialogues.text: Everyone likes a good meal, whether they're staying the night or just stopping by for a bite. We call it an inn, but the fact is, it's much more than that. We have to cater to all aspects of daily life to make this a true home away from home.

dialogues.speaker: Smiley Yanxiao
dialogues.text: Please enjoy your meal at your leisure. I should get back to work now.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Yanxiao... are you taking part in this year's Masterful Chefs?

dialogues.speaker: Smiley Yanxiao
dialogues.text: Y—You too...?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Yep, I've signed up already, and I've got my eyes on the prize! Your cooking's delicious, Yanxiao. I'm really looking forward to seeing you in the final!

dialogues.speaker: Smiley Yanxiao
dialogues.text: Hah... interesting. Alright, I'll see you there!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What was that? Some kind of power move?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: No, it seemed more sportsmanlike than that.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Yep! He's a really talented chef. His food was excellent, and it showed he has a level-headed personality. That's the kind of chef that could be a match for me.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: I haven't had any competitive cooking experience since my cook-off with Brook in Springvale.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: When the heat is on, you'll rise to the challenge!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: You're too kind... Ah!!! Guoba, what are you doing!?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Oh! Guoba's eating the...

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Those were Keqing's! How could you steal them while she wasn't looking!?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Ohh... my Golden Shrimp Balls...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Bad!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: You ate every last one... *sigh* Guoba, we've been through this. When we're with friends, you gotta be on your best behavior, okay?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: I'm so sorry, Keqing, I promise I'll make it up to you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's the big deal? We can just get another plate. After all, it's Yanxiao's treat today.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: It's not the same, though! The moment's gone. Sure, you can eat something else, but you can never go back and change that feeling of despair as your food is snatched away from right under your nose...

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: The dining experience is a trinity of emotion, food, and atmosphere, and you've gotta have all three to make it work!

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: I have to say, now that you mention it, that is a very accurate appraisal of the situation...

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: I'm gonna make it up to you, Keqing. Is there anything you wanna eat? Anything at all! Whatever it is, I'll make it for you!

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: (I don't have high hopes for this, but equally I don't want her feeling guilty... Okay, I'll let her do this for me.)

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: If you insist, there is one dish that perhaps you could try making for me. It's an old recipe from my grandfather's notes.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: No problem. May I see it?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: I'll get it to you when we're back in Liyue Harbor.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Traveler, have you finished eating?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yep.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Before we do anything else, let's head back to Liyue Harbor. I need to fetch something.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: I need to go home to fetch my grandfather's notes. Let's meet at Wanmin Restaurant later.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Great!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: I'll go get everything ready! Traveler, what about you? Are you gonna do your own thing for a while, or do you wanna come in and have a seat?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: #I actually have something to discuss with {F#her}{M#him}. You go ahead, we'll join you later.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Okay, gotcha.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Traveler, come here for a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: I need your advice on something... What do I need to do to get along with Xiangling?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Seriously? That's what's stressing you out?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: What's so strange about it? Why are you looking at me like that...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're super smart and you're always so sure of yourself. Paimon thought you'd never need advice from anyone about anything.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Well that's just ridiculous...

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Xiangling's always so warm and friendly with me, this time especially, and now she's desperate to do me a favor... So is that supposed to mean... uh, we're friends already?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: I'm just not used to dealing with people who are so warm right from the get-go. How exactly am I supposed to respond to that?

choices.text: Just smile back once in a while.

response.speaker: Keqing
response.text: Oh... um, okay...

response.speaker: Keqing
response.text: Ahem! Noted. Thank you, Traveler, I'll see you again shortly.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's making Keqing so self-conscious? Paimon thought nobody would be able to get under her skin.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'd like to hear what Xiangling thinks.

choices.text: You seem to be getting along fine already.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, we're here!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Hey, grab a seat. I'm just running through my ingredients to see what I'm missing.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Xiangling, can I ask you a question?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... we're gonna do this now?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon can explain.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But this was your idea! Why you gotta dump it on Paimon!? Urgh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, so, back at Wangshu Inn, we noticed you and Keqing were getting along pretty well. So you really like hanging out with her, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Yep! Keqing's good-natured and easy to be around. The kind of person everyone wants to know, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're a braver person than Paimon... The first time we met Keqing, Paimon found her pretty intimidating...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: She does have a formidable presence.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: You think so? I remember thinking straight away that she was really easy to get along with. Didn't you see her sneaking treats to Guoba back at Wangshu Inn?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, she's great, we know that now! We're just talking about first impressions.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: First impressions? Oh, okay — Hey, have you guys eaten grilled shellfish before? They can be hard to crack at first. But they taste amazing that way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've eaten shellfish before, but... nope, don't think we've tried eating them grilled.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Oh, you're missing out! I'll grill some for you another time. But anyway, Keqing's like a shellfish. Maybe a little closed-off at first, but once you get to know her, she's got a soft and squishy side, too!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Not to mention that even after her favorite food was stolen away, she was still happy looking after Guoba. I'm really grateful for that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You make a good point.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #You know, {NICKNAME}, Xiangling's intuition for people seems really spot-on. Is that why she took a liking to Keqing so quickly?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I think so.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Alright, let's see... We're okay for Carrots and Crab, and we still got some Ham and Mushrooms... Hmm, I wonder what Keqing's recipe is gonna be?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What was that noise!?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: What's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: What the! That bird is huge!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, it's the lady bird!

dialogues.speaker: Cloud Retainer
dialogues.text: Excuse me! One shall not be addressed in such a manner!

dialogues.speaker: Cloud Retainer
dialogues.text: One shall be known as an adeptus, whose name, should you care to mention it, is Cloud Retainer.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Cloud Retainer... that does sound like an adeptus name.

dialogues.speaker: Cloud Retainer
dialogues.text: Well spoken. One shall let this young lady's enlightened words atone for the ignorant ones of her friend.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's been a while.

dialogues.speaker: Cloud Retainer
dialogues.text: A while it has indeed been, Traveler. Does one surmise correctly that you hasten hither to partake in the Moonchase Festival?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You could put it like that, yeah...

dialogues.speaker: Cloud Retainer
dialogues.text: Ah so, even the illustrious Traveler has been summoned to attend the Moonchase Festival. As expected, this year's theme stands proud against the test of public scrutiny.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: The theme? You mean "Feast of the Bounteous Land"?

dialogues.speaker: Cloud Retainer
dialogues.text: The very same. Moonchase Festival falls during the season when many cooking ingredients are ripe, hence it is a fitting time to enjoy the finest of foods. One noticed the relative pomp and ceremony with which this year's affairs are being conducted, and could not abide to stand idly by.

dialogues.speaker: Cloud Retainer
dialogues.text: Let it be known that one's culinary proficiency and ingenuity is uncontested in all the world! Thus does one now appear in this realm, that those who inhabit it might witness one's latest creation: a supreme cuisine machine.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: A... a supreme cuisine what?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's a... supreme cuisine machine?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is it a new invention?

dialogues.speaker: Cloud Retainer
dialogues.text: Patience! One's purpose here today is to meet and to greet, nothing further. All shall be revealed before your very eyes when the time arrives.

dialogues.speaker: Cloud Retainer
dialogues.text: Traveler. You are one who has witnessed much of the culinary world. When the day comes, one would be most pleased to see you in attendance, offering your most vociferous ovations.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, so we're officially invited?

dialogues.speaker: Cloud Retainer
dialogues.text: Hmph. That which is implicitly understood needs not be made explicit, let alone official.

dialogues.speaker: Cloud Retainer
dialogues.text: I shall say no more, and dwell here no longer. Await my word! Be there or beware!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This bird always disappears just as quickly as she shows up. Wait, not bird — adeptus! ...Hey, wait, isn't she technically an illuminated bird, though...?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: She seemed like someone very prestigious, and very talented at cooking.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She definitely, definitely loves her food.
What are you all huddled together over here for? The adeptus left already.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yay, Keqing's back!

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Sorry I kept you waiting. Xiangling, this is the recipe from my grandfather's notes. They're not in the best condition, so rather than bring them out of the house, I just transcribed the recipe.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, the texts my grandfather worked with were very old — usually faded, damaged, or both. Some parts are missing from this recipe, too. Do you think you'll still be able to work with it?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Oh, okay! Lemme take a look... Hmm... Mm-hmm... Mm, mm.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Gimme some time, I need to look into it!

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Sorry for the trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Master!

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Hehe, hello Xiangling.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Madame Ping is Xiangling's master!?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: I did not expect that...

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Master, how are you keeping these days? Are you well?

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Very well, thank you. What a surprise it is that you all had the time to come and visit me today.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hi, Madame Ping!

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Hello.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Master, we came here because we have a question for you. Do you know about the Stove God?

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Of course I know the Stove God.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Does this mean... you know them personally?

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Ah, I see... it's the Moonchase Festival, isn't it.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: How interesting... Haha, so, you came to hear some stories about the Stove God?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: That's right, we're investigating something that happened recently.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: I see... The great stone surfaces, and so you open an investigation. Hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: I must commend your guesswork this far. I did indeed know the Stove God of whom you speak. But it was a great many years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Moonchase was originally a rite observed by the adepti — not something in which the ordinary people of Liyue would ever partake. But over the years they have sought to emulate it for themselves many times, giving rise to various festivals bearing the Moonchase name.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: On nights when the moon shone bright, everybody would get together for joyful reunions. There would be fine food, fine wines, and choice teas.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Later, Rex Lapis unified all of these various festivals under the Moonchase name, to honor an old friend of his. In short, the heavens were our witness as we vowed to the moon to come together in joyful solidarity, to remember the past and reflect upon the present. That is the meaning of the Moonchase Festival.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Rex Lapis... *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Hehe... That friend made many contributions to Liyue, and Rex Lapis would not have them go unrecognized. Turning this season into a commemoration of his old friend was also a way to honor that friendship.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: I can only presume that the Stove God Festival was one of the many subsumed into the Moonchase Festival.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: In the hands of Rex Lapis, our nation's traditions were faithfully upheld... It is to their detriment that we must now be the ones to inherit this duty.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Aww, Keqing...

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Oh, Keqing, I simply won't allow you to be so down on yourself. Nothing would delight Rex Lapis more than to know that those who follow in his footsteps continue to value these traditions and are working tirelessly to do them justice.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: ...Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangsheng
dialogues.text: Lady Keqing!

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangsheng
dialogues.text: Lady Keqing, Lady Ningguang wishes to speak with you.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Ningguang's looking for me?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Must be important... Please excuse me, everyone. If I'm not back soon, you'll find me at Ningguang's office.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: There she goes... Keqing's a lot more serious when she's got her work face on.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Do you want to know who Rex Lapis' friend was?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... Paimon does!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Stove God is the friend, right?

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Yes, precisely. There are few genuine coincidences in the world... the story of the lost festival and the old friend are indeed one and the same.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: The Stove God was a good friend of mine too. What a pity it is that the god is now gone both from the world and from people's memories.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: How could that happen...

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: It is to everyone's regret that the Stove God passed. But gods cannot be fully destroyed, and we made a pact to wait until the land became fruitful once more, for perhaps the Stove God would then return, albeit in a new form.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Really? ...Master, you must miss the Stove God a lot, right? From the way you talk about it all, it sounds like you were the best of friends.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Yes, thinking back on it all, there are many fond memories.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: I'm pleasantly surprised to find that Keqing is investigating this. She is a tenacious child, and anything she sets her mind to, she will diligently pursue. It warms my heart, and makes me want to give her a helping hand.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, however, I cannot simply give her the answer, for the process is of great importance to her.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Keqing's grandfather once researched the Stove God, and now she follows in his footsteps... Since Keqing has inherited this conundrum, so too she must inherit the journey to its resolution.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You knew Keqing's grandpa?

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Of course! I count all the people of Liyue among my good friends. I remember when he was the same age as Keqing is now.... Ah, so young. Hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Grandparent and grandchild are definitely made from the same mold. Both diligent enough to take on anything, and bold enough to see it through to the end.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: I like to think of Liyue as my own little potted plant. I've watched it grow and blossom, and it grows more beautiful all the time. In the blink of an eye, the buds of yesterday are in full bloom today... It's wonderful to see.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: For new blossoms must bloom on the branches if the tree is to remain evergreen and ever young.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: My dears, you are absolutely right to focus your investigation on the stone. It is, as you suppose, the lost Statue of the Stove God, and within it lie all the answers that you seek.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: I should like to see the stone for myself, if you would lead me to it. Perhaps the truth will emerge even as we watch on.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Ah, you're all here! I was just about to send someone to fetch you.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Keqing, has the stone undergone any changes?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: A crack has appeared in one corner. But we still can't tell what's inside.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What happened? Did someone chip it while no one else was looking?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: More likely a natural occurrence. Our weapons have had no effect on it.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: How would a "natural occurrence" crack it open?

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: This is because the Stove God draws power from the actions of the masses. The heat of a busy kitchen, the joy of a reunion... Haha, keep up the good work and the truth will rise to the surface soon enough.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: All the books say that the Stove God is the deity of food. So is this stone opening up because everyone's cooking for the festival?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Statues draw power from their people... so if the Stove God has dominion over cooking, could it be that the passion people put into their cooking gives power to the Stove God?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Ningguang and I chose "Feast of the Bounteous Land" as this year's theme, and now every chef signed up for the competition is busy preparing... Paimon's theory is not an unreasonable one.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Plus, a lot of families have reunion feasts around this time. With everyone back home, the whole city's bustling with people, and that adds a lot to the festive atmosphere.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So if the stone cracked because Liyue started getting festive, that must mean that when the festive fever peaks, it'll bust right open! Right?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: That's gotta be it! Right, Master?

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Hahaha, well, we'll have to see then, won't we?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Okay. The fact that cooking is involved gives us a perfect opportunity.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: The selections phase of Masterful Chefs will be held indoors and seen by only a few people, but the finals will be held outside, in public. Everyone who wants to will be able to come and watch it. The atmosphere will be incredibly lively, no question.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And when the finals end, boom! We'll get to see who the Stove God really is. Right?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: It's definitely a possibility.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Well I've already signed up, so I should be able to help!

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Yes. For a chef as accomplished as yourself, getting to the finals should be a breeze.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: All this talk of cooking competitions is making Paimon hungry... Ah, Paimon can't wait! It'd be great if Paimon could take a nap and then wake up when it's the finals!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: If you find out anything interesting, you gotta come back and tell me about it!

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Food and medicine are inextricably intertwined, you know. To give a full account of all the ways in which they are connected, why, I'd have to start that story from a long, long way back...

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: Shhhh! Nobody was asking!

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: Coconut milk... Now I want coconut milk.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Sincerely, Beidou, you misunderstand me. I have many simple pleasures — I take a stroll through Yujing Terrace and one down by the harbor every single day.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Ha. Well, everyone has their way of procrastinating, I guess.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Now, which book to read today? Aha, how about this — Chongyun, pick a book, any book, and read it out loud to me, will you? That way, I can give my mind a rest.

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Huh? Um, that's why you brought me along?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Don't like that plan? Okay, then I'll read one for you. Hmm... how about "Young and Hopelessly Smitten"?

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Xingqiu, don't you think you have one too many frivolous books in your collection...

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Okay... "A Guide to Getting Ahead in Yujing Terrace." How about this one, then?

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Ugh... Really, Xingqiu...

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Hmm... Okay... Interesting...

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Whew... This book is pretty complicated...

dialogues.speaker: Smiley Yanxiao
dialogues.text: Alright, show me how it's done!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You know, this is starting to feel like chili pepper weather. Mmm, Paimon's hungry for some fresh and fiery spicy food that let your taste buds have a blast!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #And if there's one dish that fits the bill, it's Black-Back Perch Stew! C'mon, {NICKNAME}, let's pay a visit to Wanmin Restaurant!
Help! I'm being robbed!

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Hmm? It came from that direction. Come on!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That should do it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's Yanxiao!
